data.title: Data Governance Innovations
data.description: This guide is for data operators to help them distinguish between emerging practices and structural trends.

data.title: A User's Guide to the 9Rs Framework
data.description: The 9Rs Framework provides an evidence-based model for identifying why an organization might open its data and the benefits it can yield, whether that be in producing Knowledge and Insights, Improving Brand Equity, or Establishing a License to Operate.  Readers will find a worksheet they can use to track how their project fulfills each “R.”

data.title: A User’s Guide to the Periodic Table of Open Data Elements
data.description: The User's Guide is a fillable document designed to empower data stewards and others seeking to improve data access. It can be used as a checklist and tool to weigh different elements based on their context and priorities.

data.title: Data Responsibility Journey
data.description: The Data Responsibility Journey is an assessment tool that outlines the opportunities and risks to consider at each stage of the data lifecycle when implementing a data collaborative.

data.title: How to Master the Practice of Defining Problems: Problem Definition Tool
data.description: Derived from a model developed through practice by The GovLab’s Stefaan Verhulst and Andrew Young, this tool guides practitioners through different stages to ensure that the work they conduct is as actionable as possible. It offers guidance, brainstorming exercises, and supplementary resources on problem identification; the clarification cycle; the mapping phase; the question cycle; and the change theory cycle.

data.title: People-Led Innovation Worksheet
data.description: Designed for city officials, and others seeking ways to improve people’s lives, the People-Led Innovation Worksheet provides a methodology to develop stronger problem-solving processes to approach urban challenges.

data.title: RD4C Data Ecosystem Mapping Tool
data.description: The RD4C Data Ecosystem Mapping Tool helps users identify and understand systems generating data about children to achieve insights around responsible data use, gaps and redundancies in the data, and more.

data.title: RD4C Decision Provenance Mapping
data.description: The RD4C Decision Provenance Mapping methodology provides a way for actors designing or assessing data investments for children to identify key decision points and stakeholders with the goal of improving strategies and advancing more professionally accountable data practices.

data.title: RD4C Opportunity and Risk Diagnostic
data.description: The RD4C Opportunity and Risk Diagnostic Tool provides organizations with a way to take stock of the RD4C principles and how they might be realized as an organization reviews a data project or system.

data.title: AI Localism Canvas
data.description: The canvas is a framework to help decision-makers identify, categorize and assess instances of AI Localism specific to a city or region.

data.title: Contractual Wheel of Data Collaboration
data.description: Created by the GovLab and built from an assessment of legal agreements, this wheel and C4DC’s online library of legal clauses were the bases for our analytical framework. They can also serve as a guide for users to gain a better understanding of the nature and function of data sharing agreements.

data.title: Data Collaboratives Canvas
data.description: The data collaborative canvas outlines eight phases for designing and implementing a data collaborative (partnership) at an institutional level. The online resource includes examples, enablers, tools, and resources for each phase.

data.title: Data4COVID19 Review Assessment Framework
data.description: The GovLab developed an assessment framework to evaluate how different types of non-traditional data initiatives were organized and implemented. This work is supported by a worksheet that can help assess how those initiatives performed across a specific set of criteria.

data.title: The Circular City Data Value Canvas
data.description: The GovLab developed “Data Value Canvases” to better understand the different aspects of city-centric data collaboratives. This framework explains the context of value propositions, identifies beneficiaries, highlights enabling and disabling conditions and notes proxies for monetary value.

data.title: The Data Assembly Responsible Data Re-Use Framework
data.description: The Responsible Data Re-Use Framework synthesizes lessons learned from the New York City Data Assembly and presents a set of design principles to support responsible data handling policy and practice.

data.title: Third Wave of Open Data Toolkit
data.description: The toolkit explains the complementary processes that facilitate open data and provides a series of “primers” explaining how each element of the Third Wave of Open Data manifests.

data.title: R-Search Methodology
data.description: The R-Search approach is a useful way to gain a rapid understanding of issues, scholarship, actions and opinions surrounding a topic to allow for the design of responses that are more informed and targeted.

data.title: The 100 Questions Methodology
data.description: The 100 Questions Methodology is a smarter crowdsourcing approach that uses a set of "bilinguals," experts in data science and a domain, to source questions that matter. The public then prioritizes these questions based on their individual concerns. It provides a way to create purposeful, impactful data collaboratives.

data.title: Toward An Open Data Demand Assessment And Segmentation Methodology
data.description: The GovLab, in partnership with the Inter-American Development Bank, and with the support of the French Development Agency developed the Open Data Demand and Assessment Methodology (Beta) to provide open data policymakers and practitioners with an approach for identifying, segmenting, and engaging with demand.

data.title: AI Localism Repository
data.description: A living curation of city- and state-level AI governance practices across the world.

data.title: Contracts for Data Collaboration Library
data.description: This C4DC legal agreement library hosts clauses taken from numerous data sharing agreements. Under “List of Example Agreements”, the reader can view the complete list of agreements represented in the library.

data.title: Data4COVID19 Data Collaborative Repository
data.description: A collection of almost 300 data collaboratives, data competitions, requests for proposals, and other innovative public- and private-sector data work seeking to address the pandemic.

data.title: Data4COVID Mobility Data Collaborative Repository
data.description: A collection of data collaboratives that make use of data about mobility to support decision-making regarding pandemic prevention, monitoring, and response.

data.title: Data Collaboratives Explorer
data.description: The Data Collaboratives Explorer is the largest collection of data collaboratives, a new form of collaboration, beyond the public-private partnership model, in which participants from different sectors — in particular companies — exchange their data to create public value.

data.title: State of Open Data Policy Repository
data.description: A repository of recent policy developments surrounding open data, data reuse, and data collaboration around the world. It looks specifically at how these policies can better enable a third wave of open data.

data.title: Facilitating Data Flows through Data Collaboratives
data.description: This guide provides a comprehensive overview of the key considerations and steps involved in designing and operationalizing data collaboratives. It includes recommendations for decision-makers and practical steps for practitioners.

data.title: Data Sandboxes: Managing the Open Data Spectrum
data.description: A white paper to support responsible and innovative data collaboration practices through the design, adoption, and governance of data sandboxes.

data.title: Moving From Idea to Practice: Three Resources to Streamline the Creation of Data Sharing Agreements
data.description: In February and March 2023, the Open Data Policy Lab and TrustRelay co-hosted conversations with multiple experts in law, data, and smart cities to solve this problem. The result was three documents that seek to help data stewards in the public and private sector address common barriers to forming a data sharing agreement.

data.title: Trust but Verify: A Guide to Conducting Due Diligence When Leveraging Non-Traditional Data in the Public Interest
data.description: The potential of non-traditional data for tackling societal challenges like disaster response, public healthcare, and environmental protection is promising. However, alongside these opportunities come significant ethical, legal, and operational risk. Our latest report, Trust but Verify, offers a six-step framework for conducting due diligence in non-traditional data partnerships. Authored by Sara Marcucci, Andrew J. Zahuranec, and Stefaan Verhulst, this guide is designed to help both public and private sectors navigate the ethical, legal, and practical challenges of setting up non-traditional data initiatives.

data.title: A Blueprint to Unlock New Data Commons for AI
data.description:
This Blueprint guides organizations that have or steward data on how to create new
data commons to enable public-interest AI use cases. It includes four modules, providing step by step guides on how to map the supply and demand, unlock participatory governance, build the commons, and assess and iterate.

data.title: Taxonomy of Data Commons Use Cases for AI
data.description: A supplement to "A Blueprint to Unlock New Data Commons for AI", this document provides a framework that maps the types of data useful for generative AI applications. It also outlines 10 distinct AI use cases where a data commons approach could be vaulable for society.

data.title: Data Commons Blueprint Worksheets
data.description: A supplement to the "Blueprint to Unlock New Data Commons for AI", this document provides a series of worksheets that organizations can use when creating a data commons. These correspond with each of the four modules within the blueprint.

data.title: A Facilitator’s Guide to Establishing a Social License for Data Reuse
data.description: This facilitator’s guide helps practitioners capture preferences and expectations about data reuse through engagements with communities. It includes a worksheet organized around six governance dimensions—why, what, who, how, when, and where—that can be used during discussions to inform decisions about acceptable uses, safeguards, and oversight.
